items.title: Nothing’s ANC-equipped earbuds are on sale for less than $20 for Black Friday
items.author: Brad Bourque
items.content: If our sub-$30 Black Friday roundup has you hungry for more great gadgets at low prices, you can currently grab the Nothing CMF Buds 2A in black starting at $17.89 on Amazon for Black Friday, which is about $11 less than the MSRP and the lowest price we’ve seen. The wireless earbuds are discounted in all three colors; however, the light gray and orange sets are slightly more expensive at $19.99 ($9 off). Nothing CMF Buds 2A The CMF Buds 2A deliver decent sound and noise cancellation. They also offer useful extras like customizable EQ settings, multipoint connectivity, and IP54 water and dust resistance. Where to Buy: $29 $17.89 at Amazon (black) $29 $19.99 at Amazon (white) $29 $19.99 at Amazon (orange) While they may not have the same premium features or sound as flagship budget buds like the AirPods 5 and Google’s Pixel Buds 2A, it’s hard to argue with the value. For just $20, you get active noise cancellation, support for Google Fast Pair, and up to eight hours of battery life before you need to toss them into the included USB-C charging case. My colleague Brandon Widder keeps some in his backpack as a backup pair of earbuds, and their IP54 water and dust resistance rating makes a great choice for light exercise and yard work.

items.title: Apple’s latest AirTags have dropped to just $18 a pop for Black Friday
items.author: Brad Bourque
items.content: AirTags attach easily to keyrings, luggage, and bags, provided you pair them with the right accessory. If you’re tired of constantly scrounging around for your lost belongings, Apple’s second-gen AirTags are on sale for an all-time low of $18 at Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy. The handy location trackers have a list price of $29 each, but have been consistently available for around $24 since Amazon Prime Day in late June. Apple AirTag (second-gen) Where to Buy: $29 $18 at Amazon $29 $18 at Walmart $29 $18 at Best Buy The upgraded ultra-wideband chip and improved Bluetooth in the latest AirTag should provide more precise location tracking, with a range 1.5x wider than the first-gen model. The internal speaker is also 50 percent louder than the original, making it easier to find whatever item your AirTag is attached to, whether it’s buried deep in your couch cushions or at the bottom of your bag. Even without those improvements, though, AirTags are still a great option for Apple users looking for their keys or luggage, with up to a year of battery life on a single coin cell battery and compatibility with both iPhones and newer Apple Watch models. Read our full AirTag (second-gen) review.

items.title: Inside the AI Training Data Market — Gabe Greenberg, G2i
items.author: Latent.Space
items.content: A frontier lab can pay more for training data it gets to keep exclusive, or take a discount on data another lab can buy too. At AI Engineer CODE, G2i founder Gabe Greenberg tells swyx how labs make that decision, how small pilot orders turn into bigger engagements, and when it makes sense to build a data operation in-house. We also get into what the labs are buying. A good training task should sit just ahead of what a model can do today. Gabe explains how senior engineers design the task, choose the starting data, and build a verifier that can score the result. Thanks to G2i for co-organizing AI Engineer CODE 2026 and sponsoring this episode. Join us April 26–27 at AI Engineer Miami 2027. Show notes G2i builds AI training data and reinforcement learning environments with senior engineers. ORC is the multi-agent coding platform Gabe’s team uses internally. Recorded at AI Engineer CODE in San Francisco. Chapters 0:00 How hard should training tasks be? 0:15 What G2i sells to frontier labs 2:42 From human labels to expert engineering 5:19 From recruiting engineers to building training data 6:46 Tasks, seed data, and verifiers 8:04 How G2i screens engineers for agentic work 12:24 How frontier labs buy training data 16:24 How big is the market? 18:45 Shared data, exclusivity, and in-house teams 22:16 How labs budget and price training data 24:54 The market for raw company data 27:44 Where demand goes next 30:30 G2i and ORC

items.title: The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
items.author: Sheena Vasani
items.content: I’m not saying you should read on an iPad next to fountain. I’m just saying you can. | Photo: David Pierce / The Verge We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date. iPad Mini (2026) Where to Buy: $699 $599 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 128GB) $699 $599 at Walmart (Wi-Fi, 128GB) $799 $749 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 256GB) The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game. The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify. iPad Mini (2024) Where to Buy: $599 $484 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi) $699 $584 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi) $899 $784 at Amazon (512GB, Wi-Fi) Read our full iPad Mini review.

items.content: Blade Runner 2049 looks fantastic, even if you pick up the 1080p Blu-ray version. | Image: Alcon Entertainment No shade to those who love their subscription services, but viewing physical movies is a time-honored tradition that shouldn’t go away. Watching them doesn’t feel all that different, but deciding which movie to watch feels less annoying; sifting through a movie collection on your shelf or in a storage binder is so much more fun (and less overwhelming) than scrolling endlessly in apps. While standard Blu-ray players that display movies at up to 1080p are fairly inexpensive, 4K Blu-ray counterparts that can show movies in all their 4K HDR glory are significantly pricier (but totally worth it if you’re a movie buff). No matter the player you own, there are always Blu-ray deals, and the discounts are especially good during Black Friday. items.title: Roborock, Dreame, and Eufy are cutting robovac prices in half for Black Friday
items.author: Sheena Vasani
items.content: The Eufy Omni C28 has dropped to a new low of $379.99 for Black Friday. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself. This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28, for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. If none of those are quite what you’re looking for, we’ve also found good deals on models from Roborock, Dreame, and more, with picks below for a variety of budgets and cleaning needs. Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review. Where to Buy: $999.99 $549.99 at Amazon $999.99 $549.99 at Roborock Roborock Q10 S5 Plus Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock. Where to Buy: $549.99 $229.99 at Amazon $549.99 $229.99 at Roborock Matic robot vacuum The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review. Where to Buy: $1795 $1395 at Matic (Standard Bundle) $1995 $1595 at Matic (Serene Bundle) Eufy Omni C28 The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors. Where to Buy: $799.99 $379.99 at Amazon $799.99 $379.99 at Eufy (with code WS24C28200NEW1) Dreame X60 Ultra The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets. Where to Buy: $1499.99 $999.99 at Amazon $1499.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (with Dreame W10 vacuum) $1499.99 $999.99 at Dreame Narwal Flow 2 The Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent robot vacuum for hardwood floors. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and a good vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most models. Read our review. Where to Buy: $1499.99 $899.99 at Amazon (with on-page coupon) $1499.99 $949.99 at Wayfair Roborock Saros 20 Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms. Where to Buy: $1599.99 $989.99 at Amazon $1599.99 $989.99 at Walmart $1599.99 $989.99 at Roborock Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water. Where to Buy: $1499.99 $749 at Amazon $1499.99 $749 at Best Buy Switchbot K11 Plus The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet. Where to Buy: $399.99 $169.56 at Amazon (with on-page coupon) $399.99 $160 at SwitchBot (with code BFCMX60) Dreame X50 Ultra With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less. Where to Buy: $1599.99 $799.99 at Amazon $1599.99 $799.99 at Dreame $1599.99 $799.99 at Target Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs. Where to Buy: $799.99 $474.98 at Amazon Narwal Freo X Ultra The Freo X Ultra features spinning triangular mop pads and can swing slightly to reach baseboards. Its large charging dock holds two big water tanks, while Narwal’s disposable onboard bin compresses the dust. It’s also relatively quiet when it returns to the dock, and its anti-tangle brush and 8,200Pa of suction perform well on most carpets. Where to Buy: $699.99 $399.99 at Amazon
